Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

tidydiversity 0.1.0

  • A named palette in autoplot() methods that misses a category is now an error naming the category; before, ggplot2 drew that category grey without a warning. Fully named palettes always coloured categories by name.

  • All geospatial and mapping code has moved to the companion package tidymapr: the geo_*() verbs, as_sf(), as_spat_raster(), plot_sites(), plot_geo(), plot_topo(), geo_save(), the sdm_*() functions and plot_sdm(), the spatial stem verbs stems_quadrat(), stems_habitat(), stems_neighbours() and stems_habitat_test(), the geo_example_*() helpers and the png_ants_sites coordinates. Load both packages to map diversity results; tidymapr returns the same tibbles and ggplots. tidydiversity no longer suggests any spatial package, and the map figures have left its README and website.

  • Maps now use real, published records only. New png_ants_sites holds the published bait GPS of the 16 Mt Wilhelm ant transects (Mottl, Moses and Klimes 2023, doi:10.5281/zenodo.8191946), and geo_example_sites() returns their band centroids instead of invented coordinates (the "wanang" option, which had no published coordinates, is removed). The README and the new “Maps (bonus)” section of the website Gallery show a study-site map, a Hill-number map, an SRTM elevation map and an SDM of Oecophylla smaragdina from GBIF records (CC0 / CC BY 4.0, shipped in inst/extdata/gbif_oecophylla_png.csv) and WorldClim 2.1, rendered by data-raw/gallery_maps.R. The simulated stem map and demonstration SDM figures are gone. plot_sdm() no longer adds a default “demonstration” subtitle.

  • Tile basemaps from maptiles are now projected to the map CRS and drawn the right way up, and tile zoom is chosen from the map extent so site maps are sharp.

  • Map interoperability: as_sf() and as_spat_raster() return CRS-aware sf / terra objects for optional use with tmap and leaflet (Suggests only; not hard Imports).

  • Tidy replacements for the Moses et al. (2021) Biotropica plotting stack (doi:10.1111/btp.12914): plot_partial() (visreg-like partial effects), plot_surface() (plotmo / visreg2d-like two-predictor contours), and model_count() (Poisson, quasi-Poisson, negative binomial, binomial, quasi-binomial) so callers never need visreg, plotmo or aods3.

  • Geospatial follow-up: environmental distance in geo_distance() / geo_decay() (Euclidean or Gower on bioclim columns); Hill-number site maps via plot_geo() with scale bar and north arrow; geo_elevation() (SRTM-style DEM with cache / offline path); geo_mem() (dbMEM / PCNM); geo_rarefy_spatial(); geo_grain() (MAUP / multi-grain Hill numbers); geo_middomain(); CHELSA-CMIP6 via geo_chelsa(scenario=, year=); ForestGEO stems_habitat_test() (torus); tidy SDM family sdm_fit() / sdm_predict() / sdm_evaluate() / plot_sdm() (glm, gam, native maxnet-like; no Java Maxent, no biomod2); geo_as_features() for prioritizr hand-off. Spectral / rgee remain deferred. New Rcpp kernels for Euclidean distances, neighbour counts, torus shifts, spatial rarefaction and SDM link functions.

  • ForestGEO-style census verbs: stems_as_trees(), stems_quadrat(), stems_abundance(), stems_basal_area(), stems_size_class(), stems_demography(), stems_habitat(), stems_as_community(), stems_neighbours(), plus geo_example_censuses().

  • plot_topo() maps ForestGEO-style stems (gx, gy, DBH, species) over contour and hillshade backdrops. geo_example_stems(), geo_example_dem() and geo_example_censuses() are simulated test data for checking code only; no map in the documentation is drawn from them.

  • Basemaps for plot_sites() and plot_geo() via basemap / geo_basemap() (none, coast, OSM / Carto / ESRI tiles with offline coast fallback, or a user raster). Vector verbs: geo_buffer(), geo_crop(), geo_intersection(), geo_difference(), geo_union(), geo_area(), geo_centroid(), geo_bbox(), geo_join(), geo_distance_to(). Raster verbs: geo_raster_read(), geo_raster_crop(), geo_raster_mask(), geo_raster_resample(), geo_raster_project(), geo_raster_terrain(), geo_raster_focal(), geo_raster_zonal(). Bioclimate: geo_bioclim_vars(), geo_bioclim(), geo_worldclim(), geo_chelsa() with cache and offline path (cite Fick and Hijmans 2017; Karger et al. 2017).

  • plot_sites() draws publication-ready study-site maps (grouping, labels, raster or coastline backdrop, facets, scale bar and north arrow without map-package dependencies). geo_example_sites() returns the published bait GPS positions for the Mt Wilhelm elevation bands. SDM tools such as biomod2 and Maxent remain out of scope until rebuilt as tidy verbs.

  • Geospatial workflow (native tidyverse-style verbs; sf and terra as Suggests): geo_as_sf(), geo_drop_geometry(), geo_extract(), geo_clean() (occurrence flags rebuilt so callers never need CoordinateCleaner), geo_gbif(), geo_distance(), geo_decay() (feeds beta_decay_model() with great-circle or elevational distance), plot_geo() and geo_moran() (Moran’s I with a permutation p-value, rebuilt so callers never need spdep). Compiled haversine kernels speed large distance tables. New article “Geospatial diversity workflows”.

  • Package scaffold.

  • New plots: plot_venn() draws Venn diagrams of the species shared by two to four groups; plot_phylo() draws a phylogeny with a column of relative abundances per site and can highlight the branches (Faith’s PD) of one site; plot_trait_space() places species in a PCoA trait space with each group’s convex hull (functional richness) and community-weighted mean.

  • New dataset wanang_caterpillars: 9,363 Lepidoptera larvae of 849 morphospecies reared from host trees in primary and secondary forest at Wanang (Butterill and Redmond 2023, GBIF, CC BY 4.0).

  • Citations corrected: Moses et al. (2023) pages 2212-2229, Dahl et al.

    1. volume 56 pages 90-97, the Portal Project data paper (Ernest et al. 2018, bioRxiv) and the authors and years of the Plowman et al. and Luk et al. Dryad datasets, all checked against Crossref and DataCite.

  • Input checks: beta_hill(), beta_hill_pair() and div_completeness() now reject infinite q, which used to return NaN. Bootstrapping a sample of more than 2,147,483,647 individuals now gives a clear error instead of failing inside stats::rmultinom(). div_evenness() and the other extrapolating verbs no longer fail at high q, where the asymptotic estimator is undefined; they fall back to the observed value.

  • div_completeness() warns when a sample has only singletons: estimates for q > 0 are then unreliable and can be negative (as in iNEXT.4steps).

  • tidydiversity is dedicated to the memory of Filip Damen (about 1966-2026) of Wanang Village, Papua New Guinea: a new article tells his story, linked from the navigation bar and the README.

  • beta_permanova() now defaults to by = "margin": each term is tested after all the others, so results no longer depend on the order of terms in the formula. The previous default, sequential tests (by = "terms", also vegan’s default), is still available.

  • beta_decay_model(): fits exponential or power distance-decay models of similarity to beta_decay() output and tests them by permuting sites (Mantel-style). Estimates match betapart::decay.model(); the p-value uses (1 + count) / (1 + permutations), so it is never zero.

  • beta_hill_pair(): pairwise Hill-number gamma, alpha and beta with the four normalised dissimilarities (Chao, Chiu and Jost 2014) for every pair of sites. At q = 0 it gives Sorensen and Jaccard, at q = 2 Morisita-Horn. beta_dist() and autoplot() accept its output.

  • Ordination plots and the pairwise heatmap keep a fixed aspect ratio; they now paint the whole image white, so no transparent margin is left on web pages, slides or transparent devices.

  • Plots on the website: the site’s dark mode no longer inverts figures (it turned white plots black and changed their colours); every figure is shown white with its true colours.

  • Ordination plots: all labels (species, sites, variables, centroids) are placed in one layer that avoids every point and every other label; leader lines for moved labels are faint and dotted, and no longer look like species vectors. The help page and article explain every line type. The text layer no longer adds “a” keys to the legend.

  • Coverage plots repel site labels instead of overprinting them and show no axis tick above 100%; facet panels have more space between them.

  • beta_indicator() now corrects p-values for multiple testing (adjust = "holm" by default; new column p.adj) and selects species on the adjusted values. Use adjust = "none" for the previous behaviour.

  • autoplot() for beta_hill() results: gamma, alpha and beta, or the four dissimilarities, against q with bootstrap intervals.

  • Website: every figure, including reference-page examples, now has an opaque white background, so no plot turns dark in the site’s dark mode. New gallery entry, README tables and text for beta_hill() and beta_welch().

  • beta_welch(): Welch-type PERMANOVA (W*d; Hamidi et al. 2019), robust to unequal dispersion; equals Welch’s F in one Euclidean dimension.

  • beta_hill(): coverage-standardised gamma, alpha and beta Hill numbers with four normalised dissimilarities (Chao et al. 2023), for taxonomic, phylogenetic (type = "PD") and functional (type = "FD", threshold or AUC) diversity, abundance or incidence (unit) data, and bootstrap confidence intervals (nboot); point estimates match iNEXT.beta3D exactly.

  • Trait-based ecology, following the Handbook of Trait-Based Ecology (de Bello et al. 2021): trait_dist() (Gower, gawdis), trait_cwm(), trait_cwm_test() (max test), trait_fd_indices() (FRic, FEve, FDiv, FDis, Rao), trait_rao() (alpha/beta/gamma with equivalent numbers), trait_ses() (null models), trait_itv() (intra- vs interspecific variability) and trait_fourth_corner(). data_aravo() loads the ade4 alpine plant data. Trait probability densities (trait_tpd(), trait_tpd_dissim(), computed natively after TPD::TPDs()), and phylogenetic signal (phylo_signal(), with a fast native Blomberg’s K), phylo_dist() and phylo_combine_dist(). New article “Trait-based ecology”.

  • Testing community composition: beta_permanova() (PERMANOVA, with restricted permutations), beta_dispersion() (homogeneity of dispersion, with autoplot()), ord_select() (forward selection with double stopping), ord_varpart() (variation partitioning with tests) and beta_indicator() (indicator species). Results match vegan and indicspecies exactly. New article “Testing community composition”.

  • tidymodels integration: model_group_folds() (site-blocked cross-validation), model_case_weights() (inverse-variance weights from diversity SEs) and the recipe step step_hill(). New article “Modelling diversity with tidymodels”.

  • Multi-panel figures: plot_panel() combines plots with patchwork, adding panel tags (a, b, …), shared legends and white backgrounds; plot_save() saves at journal column widths (85, 120 or 175 mm) and 300 dpi.

  • Ordination: ord_fit() fits PCA, CA, DCA, PCoA, NMDS, RDA, CCA and db-RDA (with partial versions through Condition()) to long community data with vegan, returning tidy scores; results match vegan exactly. Variables are fitted passively to unconstrained ordinations, as in CANOCO. ord_test() gives tidy permutation tests, and autoplot() draws CANOCO-style biplots and triplots with ellipses, hulls, spiders and non-overlapping labels. New article “Ordination: biplots and triplots”.

  • wanang_butterflies combines three species that the source spreadsheet listed in two columns each (189 species, counts unchanged).

  • png_ants leaves out its single dry-season record at 2700 m, so both seasons cover the same five elevations (200 to 2200 m) and can be compared directly.

  • Plots no longer print “Ignoring unknown labels” messages, and long site legends wrap instead of running off the figure.

  • Incidence data for TD, PD and FD: div_hill(), div_estimate(), div_coverage(), div_rarefy() and div_standardise() gain unit (the sampling-unit column) and n_units (units sampled, including empty ones). Estimates, rarefaction, extrapolation, coverage and bootstrap intervals are incidence-based (Chao et al. 2014); for PD a branch is present in a unit when any species below it was detected. Results match iNEXT.3D on its fish survey and iNEXT on the png_ants baits.

  • png_ants gains baits, the number of baits set at each elevation and season, for incidence-based estimates with unit = bait.

  • Example data are now real, published field data from Papua New Guinea, replacing the simulated ant_gradient: png_ants (ants at nutrient baits along Mt Wilhelm; Moses et al. 2023), png_tree_ants (tree-nesting ants in three plots; Plowman et al. 2020), png_frogs (frogs along Mt Wilhelm; Dahl et al. 2024) and wanang_butterflies (butterfly monitoring at Wanang; Luk et al. 2019). Each is rebuilt from its Zenodo deposit by a script in data-raw/.

  • New case-study articles for the Papua New Guinea ants, frogs and butterflies.

  • Rarefaction and extrapolation are about 60 times faster on large samples, with identical results.

  • Phylogenetic (PD) and functional (FD) diversity: div_hill(), div_estimate(), div_rarefy() and div_standardise() gain type = c("TD", "PD", "FD") with tree, reftime, pd_unit, distance and tau (including tau = "auc"). Point estimates match iNEXT.3D to within 1e-6.

  • Bootstrap standard errors and confidence intervals for PD and FD in div_estimate(), div_standardise() and div_rarefy(), previously NA. The bootstrap community adds undetected species with estimated branch lengths (PD) or distances (FD).

  • New article “TD, PD and FD on one scale”, and a rewritten home page.

  • div_completeness() and div_evenness() give sample completeness and evenness profiles (classes E1 to E5) that match iNEXT.4steps.

  • autoplot() methods for every result type: div_hill() profiles and gradients, div_estimate(), div_coverage(), beta_pair() heatmaps and beta_multi() stacked bars.

Developed by Jimmy Moses.
